explanation: With no pockets in a kimono, men hung tobacco pouches and small boxes called inrō on a cord from the sash; the netsuke, wedged above it, stopped the cord slipping.

claims.text: Netsuke were toggles used to secure pouches, boxes such as inrō and other hanging containers on a cord from a kimono sash.
Netsuke were not used to hang swords, folding fans or prayer bells.
Traditional kimono have no pockets in the Western sense, so men hung containers from the sash.
The netsuke sat above the sash and stopped the cord from slipping through.
